text:
## Abstract

This report resolves GEO series GSE309890 to its underlying raw sequencing reads and evaluates whether a genome assembly is the appropriate analysis. GSE309890 is a study of sertraline-biased antibiotic resistance in *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655, comprising 6 samples. Routing from GEO to its linked BioProject (PRJNA1363958 / SRA study SRP644513) recovered 6 sequencing runs, all publicly downloadable as paired-end FASTQ from ENA. The critical finding for the stated goal is the library type: all 6 runs are RNA-Seq (LibrarySource TRANSCRIPTOMIC, LibrarySelection cDNA), sequenced on Illumina HiSeq 4000 at 2×150 (avgLength 300, paired), totalling roughly 20.8 billion bases across 69.1 million read pairs. A de novo genome assembly is not the correct workflow for cDNA reads; the reads sample expressed transcripts, not the whole genome uniformly. The IWC/BRC workflow catalog offers a single Assembly workflow (long-read polishing only, requiring Sanger/long reads these Illumina data are not), whereas the Transcriptomics category contains an RNA-Seq paired-end workflow that matches these libraries and the available complete reference genome (GCF_000005845.2, 4,641,652 bp, haploid). The reads are fully retrievable; the appropriate analysis is reference-based RNA-Seq quantification, or optionally de novo transcriptome assembly, rather than genome assembly.

## I. Introduction

**Background.** GSE309890 profiles *E. coli* K-12 MG1655 adapting to the SSRI sertraline, testing how stress rewires the pentose phosphate pathway and biases resistance emergence. The experiment is "Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing" with 6 samples: three controls and three 40-day adaptive-evolution replicates.

**Literature Review.** No literature was retrieved for this query. GEO reports no PubMed record linked to GSE309890 (the tool notes this typically indicates an unpublished or not-yet-indexed study, not absence of data).

**Knowledge Gap.** Before querying it was unknown (a) whether raw reads are public and downloadable, and (b) whether the library type supports a genome assembly.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** Objective: obtain the raw reads behind GSE309890 and determine whether they can be assembled. Testable expectation: if the libraries are transcriptomic cDNA rather than genomic DNA, a de novo genome assembly is not the appropriate workflow.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** I routed GEO → linked BioProject/SRA (for run-level library metadata) → ENA (for working download URLs) → BRC Analytics assembly/workflow catalog (to test assembly feasibility against the reference genome and available pipelines).

**Materials.** NCBI GEO (`geo_series`); NCBI SRA (`ncbi_sra_runs_for_project`); NCBI Taxonomy (`ncbi_taxonomy_lookup`); BRC Analytics assemblies and workflows (`get_assemblies`, `list_workflow_categories`, `get_workflows_in_category`); ENA (`brc_ena_study`).

**Procedures.**
1. `geo_series(accession="GSE309890")` → BioProject PRJNA1363958, 6 samples, taxon *E. coli* K-12 MG1655.
2. `ncbi_sra_runs_for_project(accession="PRJNA1363958", max_results=50)` → 6 runs with library metadata.
3. `ncbi_taxonomy_lookup(query="Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655")` → taxid 511145.
4. `get_assemblies(taxonomy_id="511145")` → 1 reference assembly.
5. `list_workflow_categories()` and `get_workflows_in_category` for `ASSEMBLY` and `TRANSCRIPTOMICS`.
6. `brc_ena_study(study_accession="PRJNA1363958")` → FASTQ HTTPS links.

**Statistical Analysis.** Run count (6) is the SRA record count for the BioProject. Base and read totals are summed across the 6 runs from the SRA `bases` and `spots` fields. Library classification is read directly from the SRA `LibraryStrategy`/`LibrarySource`/`LibrarySelection` fields (identical across all 6 runs). No deduplication was required; run accessions are unique.

## III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

**Table 1. Raw sequencing runs for GSE309890 (BioProject PRJNA1363958 / SRP644513).**

| Run | GEO sample | Condition | Strategy | Layout | Read pairs | Bases | R1 / R2 FASTQ (HTTPS) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SRR36018640 | GSM9284462 | adaptive evo 40d rep3 | RNA-Seq | PAIRED | 11,363,329 | 3,408,998,700 | .../SRR360/040/SRR36018640/SRR36018640_1.fastq.gz ; _2 |
| SRR36018641 | GSM9284461 | adaptive evo 40d rep2 | RNA-Seq | PAIRED | 11,997,182 | 3,599,154,600 | .../SRR360/041/SRR36018641/SRR36018641_1.fastq.gz ; _2 |
| SRR36018642 | GSM9284460 | adaptive evo 40d rep1 | RNA-Seq | PAIRED | 11,992,461 | 3,597,738,300 | .../SRR360/042/SRR36018642/SRR36018642_1.fastq.gz ; _2 |
| SRR36018643 | GSM9284459 | control rep3 | RNA-Seq | PAIRED | 11,720,219 | 3,516,065,700 | .../SRR360/043/SRR36018643/SRR36018643_1.fastq.gz ; _2 |
| SRR36018644 | GSM9284458 | control rep2 | RNA-Seq | PAIRED | 10,415,434 | 3,124,630,200 | .../SRR360/044/SRR36018644/SRR36018644_1.fastq.gz ; _2 |
| SRR36018645 | GSM9284457 | control rep1 | RNA-Seq | PAIRED | 11,621,726 | 3,486,517,800 | .../SRR360/045/SRR36018645/SRR36018645_1.fastq.gz ; _2 |

Full URLs (example R1/R2 for SRR36018640): `https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/040/SRR36018640/SRR36018640_1.fastq.gz` and `.../SRR36018640_2.fastq.gz`. All other runs follow the identical path pattern shown in the table.

**Table 2. Assembly feasibility against BRC catalog.**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Reference genome available | GCF_000005845.2 (ASM584v2), Complete Genome, 4,641,652 bp, 1 chromosome, haploid |
| Gene model (GTF) | GCF_000005845.2_ASM584v2.ncbiGene.gtf.gz |
| Assembly workflows in catalog | 1 (`polish-with-long-reads-main`; requires long/Sanger reads) |
| Transcriptomics workflows | 4, incl. `rnaseq-pe-main` (RNA-Seq, PAIRED — matches these data) |
| Library type of GSE309890 reads | RNA-Seq / TRANSCRIPTOMIC / cDNA (all 6 runs) |

**Findings.** All 6 runs are public paired-end Illumina HiSeq 4000 RNA-Seq libraries, retrievable from ENA. The dataset totals 69,110,351 read pairs and 20,733,105,300 bases. The only assembly workflow in the catalog accepts long reads for polishing, not Illumina short reads; it does not fit these data. One transcriptomics workflow (`rnaseq-pe-main`) matches the library layout (PAIRED) and strategy (RNA-Seq) and pairs with the single available reference genome and gene model.

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** Yes, you can get the raw reads — all six FASTQ files are public and directly downloadable from ENA (Table 1). However, "run an assembly on them" is a mismatch with the data. These are cDNA/RNA-Seq libraries: coverage is proportional to transcript abundance, not uniform across the genome, so a de novo *genome* assembler would produce a fragmented, expression-biased result rather than a genome. The objective's assembly premise is therefore not met by this dataset.

**Context.** The study is itself an expression-profiling experiment (control vs. 40-day adaptive-evolution replicates), consistent with the RNA-Seq library type. The matching route is reference-based RNA-Seq quantification against the complete MG1655 reference (GCF_000005845.2) using `rnaseq-pe-main` — which reproduces the same class of output (FPKMs) that GSE309890 itself deposited as a supplementary file (`GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz`).

**Limitations.** GEO/SRA report no linked publication, so I could not corroborate library prep from a methods section. The reads are avgLength 300 for paired runs (i.e., ~2×150); exact read length per mate and strandedness were not confirmed from a FastQC-level check. `insert size` is reported as 0 (not provided by submitter). If your actual goal is a *transcriptome* assembly (e.g., Trinity), that is feasible with these reads but is not in the BRC catalog and was not tested here. Assembly-workflow compatibility was assessed from catalog metadata, not by running a workflow.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** The reads are fully available; a genome assembly is not the right analysis for RNA-Seq cDNA. The next query worth running: `resolve_workflow_inputs(iwc_id="rnaseq-pe-main", accession="GCF_000005845.2")` to prefill the reference genome and gene model and confirm which inputs you must supply (the six FASTQ pairs). If a genome is genuinely needed, search SRA/ENA for a WGS (genomic DNA) library of the same strain instead.

## References

1. NCBI GEO — GSE309890: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
2. NCBI SRA (runs for PRJNA1363958), E-utilities esearch: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi?term=PRJNA1363958&retmax=50&retstart=0&sort=relevance&usehistory=y&retmode=json&db=sra&tool=fdea-ncbi-mcp&email=jonathangunti%40gmail.com
3. NCBI Taxonomy — taxid 511145: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?id=511145&retmode=xml&db=taxonomy&tool=fdea-ncbi-mcp&email=jonathangunti%40gmail.com
4. ENA Portal API — filereport for PRJNA1363958: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/filereport?accession=PRJNA1363958
5. GEO FTP supplementary directory (FPKM matrix): https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/
6. BRC Analytics — reference assembly GCF_000005845.2 gene model: https://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/hubs/GCF/000/005/845/GCF_000005845.2/genes/GCF_000005845.2_ASM584v2.ncbiGene.gtf.gz

## Acknowledgments

Data providers: NCBI GEO and SRA; the European Nucleotide Archive (EMBL-EBI); NCBI Taxonomy; the submitting center Beijing Normal University; and BRC Analytics / IWC for the reference assembly and workflow catalog.

## Abstract

This report resolves GEO series GSE309890 to its underlying raw sequencing reads and evaluates whether a genome assembly is the appropriate analysis. GSE309890 is a study of sertraline-biased antibiotic resistance in *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655, comprising 6 samples. Routing from GEO to its linked BioProject (PRJNA1363958 / SRA study SRP644513) recovered 6 sequencing runs, all publicly downloadable as paired-end FASTQ from ENA. The critical finding for the stated goal is the library type: all 6 runs are RNA-Seq (LibrarySource TRANSCRIPTOMIC, LibrarySelection cDNA), sequenced on Illumina HiSeq 4000 at 2×150 (avgLength 300, paired), totalling roughly 20.8 billion bases across 69.1 million read pairs. A de novo genome assembly is not the correct workflow for cDNA reads; the reads sample expressed transcripts, not the whole genome uniformly. The IWC/BRC workflow catalog offers a single Assembly workflow (long-read polishing only, requiring Sanger/long reads these Illumina data are not), whereas the Transcriptomics category contains an RNA-Seq paired-end workflow that matches these libraries and the available complete reference genome (GCF_000005845.2, 4,641,652 bp, haploid). The reads are fully retrievable; the appropriate analysis is reference-based RNA-Seq quantification, or optionally de novo transcriptome assembly, rather than genome assembly.

## I. Introduction

**Background.** GSE309890 profiles *E. coli* K-12 MG1655 adapting to the SSRI sertraline, testing how stress rewires the pentose phosphate pathway and biases resistance emergence. The experiment is "Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing" with 6 samples: three controls and three 40-day adaptive-evolution replicates.

**Literature Review.** No literature was retrieved for this query. GEO reports no PubMed record linked to GSE309890 (the tool notes this typically indicates an unpublished or not-yet-indexed study, not absence of data).

**Knowledge Gap.** Before querying it was unknown (a) whether raw reads are public and downloadable, and (b) whether the library type supports a genome assembly.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** Objective: obtain the raw reads behind GSE309890 and determine whether they can be assembled. Testable expectation: if the libraries are transcriptomic cDNA rather than genomic DNA, a de novo genome assembly is not the appropriate workflow.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** I routed GEO → linked BioProject/SRA (for run-level library metadata) → ENA (for working download URLs) → BRC Analytics assembly/workflow catalog (to test assembly feasibility against the reference genome and available pipelines).

**Materials.** NCBI GEO (`geo_series`); NCBI SRA (`ncbi_sra_runs_for_project`); NCBI Taxonomy (`ncbi_taxonomy_lookup`); BRC Analytics assemblies and workflows (`get_assemblies`, `list_workflow_categories`, `get_workflows_in_category`); ENA (`brc_ena_study`).

**Procedures.**
1. `geo_series(accession="GSE309890")` → BioProject PRJNA1363958, 6 samples, taxon *E. coli* K-12 MG1655.
2. `ncbi_sra_runs_for_project(accession="PRJNA1363958", max_results=50)` → 6 runs with library metadata.
3. `ncbi_taxonomy_lookup(query="Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655")` → taxid 511145.
4. `get_assemblies(taxonomy_id="511145")` → 1 reference assembly.
5. `list_workflow_categories()` and `get_workflows_in_category` for `ASSEMBLY` and `TRANSCRIPTOMICS`.
6. `brc_ena_study(study_accession="PRJNA1363958")` → FASTQ HTTPS links.

**Statistical Analysis.** Run count (6) is the SRA record count for the BioProject. Base and read totals are summed across the 6 runs from the SRA `bases` and `spots` fields. Library classification is read directly from the SRA `LibraryStrategy`/`LibrarySource`/`LibrarySelection` fields (identical across all 6 runs). No deduplication was required; run accessions are unique.

## III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

**Table 1. Raw sequencing runs for GSE309890 (BioProject PRJNA1363958 / SRP644513).**

| Run | GEO sample | Condition | Strategy | Layout | Read pairs | Bases | R1 / R2 FASTQ (HTTPS) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SRR36018640 | GSM9284462 | adaptive evo 40d rep3 | RNA-Seq | PAIRED | 11,363,329 | 3,408,998,700 | .../SRR360/040/SRR36018640/SRR36018640_1.fastq.gz ; _2 |
| SRR36018641 | GSM9284461 | adaptive evo 40d rep2 | RNA-Seq | PAIRED | 11,997,182 | 3,599,154,600 | .../SRR360/041/SRR36018641/SRR36018641_1.fastq.gz ; _2 |
| SRR36018642 | GSM9284460 | adaptive evo 40d rep1 | RNA-Seq | PAIRED | 11,992,461 | 3,597,738,300 | .../SRR360/042/SRR36018642/SRR36018642_1.fastq.gz ; _2 |
| SRR36018643 | GSM9284459 | control rep3 | RNA-Seq | PAIRED | 11,720,219 | 3,516,065,700 | .../SRR360/043/SRR36018643/SRR36018643_1.fastq.gz ; _2 |
| SRR36018644 | GSM9284458 | control rep2 | RNA-Seq | PAIRED | 10,415,434 | 3,124,630,200 | .../SRR360/044/SRR36018644/SRR36018644_1.fastq.gz ; _2 |
| SRR36018645 | GSM9284457 | control rep1 | RNA-Seq | PAIRED | 11,621,726 | 3,486,517,800 | .../SRR360/045/SRR36018645/SRR36018645_1.fastq.gz ; _2 |

Full URLs (example R1/R2 for SRR36018640): `https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/040/SRR36018640/SRR36018640_1.fastq.gz` and `.../SRR36018640_2.fastq.gz`. All other runs follow the identical path pattern shown in the table.

**Table 2. Assembly feasibility against BRC catalog.**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Reference genome available | GCF_000005845.2 (ASM584v2), Complete Genome, 4,641,652 bp, 1 chromosome, haploid |
| Gene model (GTF) | GCF_000005845.2_ASM584v2.ncbiGene.gtf.gz |
| Assembly workflows in catalog | 1 (`polish-with-long-reads-main`; requires long/Sanger reads) |
| Transcriptomics workflows | 4, incl. `rnaseq-pe-main` (RNA-Seq, PAIRED — matches these data) |
| Library type of GSE309890 reads | RNA-Seq / TRANSCRIPTOMIC / cDNA (all 6 runs) |

**Findings.** All 6 runs are public paired-end Illumina HiSeq 4000 RNA-Seq libraries, retrievable from ENA. The dataset totals 69,110,351 read pairs and 20,733,105,300 bases. The only assembly workflow in the catalog accepts long reads for polishing, not Illumina short reads; it does not fit these data. One transcriptomics workflow (`rnaseq-pe-main`) matches the library layout (PAIRED) and strategy (RNA-Seq) and pairs with the single available reference genome and gene model.

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** Yes, you can get the raw reads — all six FASTQ files are public and directly downloadable from ENA (Table 1). However, "run an assembly on them" is a mismatch with the data. These are cDNA/RNA-Seq libraries: coverage is proportional to transcript abundance, not uniform across the genome, so a de novo *genome* assembler would produce a fragmented, expression-biased result rather than a genome. The objective's assembly premise is therefore not met by this dataset.

**Context.** The study is itself an expression-profiling experiment (control vs. 40-day adaptive-evolution replicates), consistent with the RNA-Seq library type. The matching route is reference-based RNA-Seq quantification against the complete MG1655 reference (GCF_000005845.2) using `rnaseq-pe-main` — which reproduces the same class of output (FPKMs) that GSE309890 itself deposited as a supplementary file (`GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz`).

**Limitations.** GEO/SRA report no linked publication, so I could not corroborate library prep from a methods section. The reads are avgLength 300 for paired runs (i.e., ~2×150); exact read length per mate and strandedness were not confirmed from a FastQC-level check. `insert size` is reported as 0 (not provided by submitter). If your actual goal is a *transcriptome* assembly (e.g., Trinity), that is feasible with these reads but is not in the BRC catalog and was not tested here. Assembly-workflow compatibility was assessed from catalog metadata, not by running a workflow.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** The reads are fully available; a genome assembly is not the right analysis for RNA-Seq cDNA. The next query worth running: `resolve_workflow_inputs(iwc_id="rnaseq-pe-main", accession="GCF_000005845.2")` to prefill the reference genome and gene model and confirm which inputs you must supply (the six FASTQ pairs). If a genome is genuinely needed, search SRA/ENA for a WGS (genomic DNA) library of the same strain instead.

## References

1. NCBI GEO — GSE309890: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
2. NCBI SRA (runs for PRJNA1363958), E-utilities esearch: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi?term=PRJNA1363958&retmax=50&retstart=0&sort=relevance&usehistory=y&retmode=json&db=sra&tool=fdea-ncbi-mcp&email=jonathangunti%40gmail.com
3. NCBI Taxonomy — taxid 511145: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?id=511145&retmode=xml&db=taxonomy&tool=fdea-ncbi-mcp&email=jonathangunti%40gmail.com
4. ENA Portal API — filereport for PRJNA1363958: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/filereport?accession=PRJNA1363958
5. GEO FTP supplementary directory (FPKM matrix): https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/
6. BRC Analytics — reference assembly GCF_000005845.2 gene model: https://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/hubs/GCF/000/005/845/GCF_000005845.2/genes/GCF_000005845.2_ASM584v2.ncbiGene.gtf.gz

Data providers: NCBI GEO and SRA; the European Nucleotide Archive (EMBL-EBI); NCBI Taxonomy; the submitting center Beijing Normal University; and BRC Analytics / IWC for the reference assembly and workflow catalog.
